definitions.explanation: The ability of different systems, devices, or components to work together or be used interchangeably.

examples.japanese: この{部品|ぶひん}は{旧|きゅう}モデルとの{互換性|ごかんせい}がない。
examples.english: This part is not compatible with the old model.

examples.japanese: {後方|こうほう}{互換性|ごかんせい}を{維持|いじ}することが{重要|じゅうよう}だ。
examples.english: It's important to maintain backward compatibility.

notes:
{互換性|ごかんせい} refers to the ability of systems, devices, or components to work together or be substituted for one another. Primarily used in technical, IT, and engineering contexts.

FORMS:
{互換|ごかん} (interchangeability) + {性|せい} (quality/property).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {互換性|ごかんせい}がある/ない: to have/lack compatibility
- {互換性|ごかんせい}を{維持|いじ}する: to maintain compatibility
- {互換性|ごかんせい}を{確保|かくほ}する: to ensure compatibility

COMPOUNDS:
- {後方|こうほう}{互換性|ごかんせい}: backward compatibility
- {前方|ぜんぽう}{互換性|ごかんせい}: forward compatibility
- {上位|じょうい}{互換|ごかん}: upward compatibility
- {下位|かい}{互換|ごかん}: downward compatibility

REGISTER:
Technical/formal. In everyday speech, people are more likely to say {使|つか}える (can use it) or {対応|たいおう}している (it supports/is compatible) rather than {互換性|ごかんせい}がある.
